name: Slow-Cooker Pork Carnitas (Monday Plates + Taco Tuesday)
description: Citrus-and-garlic pork shoulder that goes in the slow cooker at lunch and makes two dinners: Monday it's served as plates with sweet potatoes and green beans, Tuesday the leftovers get crisped under the broiler for tacos.
time: 15 minutes hands-on, 6–7 hours on low (or 4–5 on high)
ingredients: 4 lb boneless pork shoulder (pork butt), cut into 3-inch chunks
Monday sides: 3 sweet potatoes cut into wedges, 1 lb green beans, olive oil, salt
Tuesday tacos: taco tortillas, pico, black beans, Spanish rice, shredded cheese, sour cream, lime wedges
instructions: Mix the salt, cumin, chili powder, oregano, and pepper. Rub all over the pork.
Put the onion and garlic in the slow cooker, pork on top. Pour over the orange juice, lime juice, and broth; tuck in the squeezed orange halves and bay leaves.
Cook on low 6–7 hours (or high 4–5) until the pork shreds easily with a fork.

Monday: about 40 minutes before dinner, toss the sweet potato wedges with oil and salt and roast at 425°F for 30–35 minutes, adding the green beans for the last 15. Shred half the pork, moisten with a few spoonfuls of the cooking liquid, and serve.
Refrigerate the other half of the pork in some of its liquid for Tuesday.

Tuesday: spread the cold pork on a sheet pan, drizzle with a little liquid, and broil 4–6 minutes until the edges crisp. Stir, broil 2 more minutes. Fill tortillas and serve with pico, beans, and rice.
tips: Get it in before you leave for appointments; it needs no attention until dinner.
The broiler step is what makes it carnitas — don't skip it, but watch it closely.
For the toddler, pull pork before broiling so it stays soft; shred finely for the baby if they're on table foods.
Leftover cooking liquid freezes well for soups or rice.
